correctness.rationale: Over F_7 the derivative equations force contradictory Y³=2 and Y³=5 at any hypothetical geometric singularity. The twelve normalized tangent equations cover coordinate points and all nonzero coordinates by square/nonsquare cases; 57 ambient points have incidence (36,9,9,3). Hasse gives an F_7 rational origin on every smooth genus-one cubic; Pic^3(E)(F_7) is represented by 2O+T, with the exhibited basis giving an exhaustive short-Weierstrass plane model. Independently reran all 42 nonsingular (a,b), 336 (E,T) complete-series representatives: exactly eight covering models, all a=b=0,1 respectively and T with nonzero ordinate. The E_{0,1}(F_7) group is Z/6⊕Z/2, so 3E is its four rational 2-torsion points; translations by 3E and rational j=0 automorphisms act transitively on the eight non-2-torsion T, completing projective uniqueness. Degree <3 exclusion uses rational tangent-line coverage of a line/conic. Finite census is exhaustive only because of Picard-normal-form proof.

value.rationale: The classification of a natural extremal finite-geometric condition is a complete, motivated structural result, not merely another model or a finite-number table: it explains why a 12-line minimum blocking arrangement is forced to one cubic embedding class and why none has a rational flex. It can be used to identify any other tangent-filling smooth cubic over F_7 or distinguish smooth from singular cases.

final_claim: Over F_7 the explicit nonsingular cubic XY²-X²Z-2YZ² is tangent-filling; all geometrically smooth tangent-filling cubic plane models are F_7-projectively equivalent to it. The tangent incidence spectrum is 36,9,9,3 and the class has no rational flex. Degree three is minimal, already known previously.
limitations: Only geometrically smooth cubic models over the prime field F_7 are classified; not extension fields or singular cubic classes.
Rational projective equivalence and rational flex use the finite elliptic group action.
Arithmetic scripts alone do not prove Pic^3 exhaustiveness or geometric smoothness.
